label: Root links from Alexander Bird, Antidotes all the way down? Theoria 19
summary: §6, pp.267–268, dispositional essentialism and laws: Bird proposes explaining suitable laws through dispositions essential to natural properties and conditions for their manifestation. This is a rival account of lawhood to best-system regularities. Applying it to the same laws would require defending dispositional essentialism and the specified exception conditions. No defeat of best-system lawhood is asserted. §§1–3 and §§6–7, pp.259–262 and 268–269: Bird's fink and antidote cases show that possession of a disposition can fail to yield manifestation in the triggering conditions. This matters when treating the case's possession and exercise predicates as equivalent. The inverse from power to causing needs a manifestation bridge free of the relevant blockers.
